calibration_reasoning: Won on the first attempt with two player faints. AGENTS.md's review threshold at fewer than three faints applies, so I reviewed it and am recording the justified exception: this is a casual-class trainer, the lowest difficulty class in the range, and it still took Rillaboom and Incineroar - two of the six best answers available at cap 48 - off a fully optimized party in four turns. The brief's 'won with 2+ faints or after a real fight - keep' applies and a casual trainer costing two premium bodies does not need a level. No change.
could_this_be_cooler: Keep the fossil-and-shell room; for a casual trainer it is tidy and Galvanize is doing honest work rather than sitting unused. But this is the fourth encounter in this block where the designated setup piece never set up, and Garrison shows the sharpest version of it: Carracosta's White Herb was spent on turn zero erasing an opposing Intimidate, before the Shell Smash it exists to enable was ever an option. The dossier already flags the cause - 'four slow bodies with no Fake Out means the boost is always taken in the open' - and this run adds a second, cheaper cause on top: the Herb is a one-shot resource that any opposing Intimidate consumes for free. Either give the room one turn-buying move, or accept that Carracosta is a Sturdy body rather than a setup sweeper and say so in the guide. Flagged rather than changed at this class, exactly as the dossier concluded. No species, move, item or EV change recommended.
legality_problems_found: None. Carracosta's item reading NONE at turn 0 is the White Herb correctly consumed by Intimidate on entry, not a materialization fault.
